findings.message: Capacity qualification blocks recovery after a published pass followed by a technical admission failure.
findings.rationale: For pass attempt 1 → published admission failure 2 → new attempt 3, this reconstruction retains admissionFailures but sets status from qualified reviews alone, producing passed. mergeTaskSummary subsequently validates that reconstructed baseline and rejects it because the unresolved admission requires failed status. The new attempt therefore fails qualification before it can supersede the admission failure. Preserve admission-aware status when constructing the capacity baseline. The admission-history test manually installs the successful successor and bypasses this qualification path; capacity tests do not cover this sequence.

findings.message: Technical admission publication can overwrite an unsupported permanent CR version.
findings.rationale: Unlike normal publication, this branch never checks the existing head's schemaVersion. An existing schemaVersion 99 head with an otherwise readable task-based body is accepted, augmented and rewritten. ArtifactStore applies the CR codec's contentMeta, replacing its version with 3. Neither the shared decoder nor store supplies the missing version guard. This silently downgrades unsupported history instead of preserving its bytes. The existing unknown-version publication regression exercises only qualified publication; add the terminal-admission variant.

findings.message: Check controller ownership before advancing an existing review to another attempt.
findings.rationale: The next-attempt branch forwards review.worker.advance and closes the previous worker before reaching assertController. Once the previous controller attempt is terminal and eligible to advance, another live connection can submit attempt N+1, retire that owner's worker, and acquire the replacement. The private call uses the previous owner's trusted context, so the worker cannot detect the foreign initiator. This bypasses the required owner check before forwarding. Existing wrong-owner assertions cover progress/result exchanges, but not next-attempt admission.

findings.message: Reclaim terminal workers before retaining their design-subject exclusion indefinitely.
findings.rationale: The subject exclusion considers every registry entry, including completed or failed reviews. Terminal progress only updates the cache/status board; neither it nor the worker runtime initiates normal terminal reclamation. Consequently, a completed daemon design review continues blocking a fresh review ID for the same artifact until cleanup, explicit replacement, or daemon shutdown. It also retains the worker's live ports/thread. The LLD requires terminal drain and reclamation, and the family coordinator releases its own subject lease after execution. Tests assert active-subject exclusion but do not attempt a fresh same-subject review after completion.

tasks.summary: Completed inspection of all submitted changed segments, the pinned requirements/design and relevant test assertions. Found three recovery defects affecting cold publication retries, rejected restarts and reviewer changes.

findings.message: Cold publication retries still create an unverified execution-recovery action.
findings.rationale: After worker exit, the public design recover route boots a regular worker and reaches this unconditional admitDesignRecovery call for retry_publication. DesignReviewWorker.recover then takes its publication-only branch without settling that action. This changes the preservation digest of already accepted feedback, so lost-receipt publication cannot locate its original history entry and fails the unchanged-subject check. The lingering unverified action also blocks subsequent new recovery actions. The publication tests exercise cold registry.publishStored maintenance workers and live public retries, leaving this cold public route uncovered.

findings.message: A rejected full restart permanently advances the live attempt identity.
findings.rationale: resultAttempt is calculated before qualification, and both targetAttempt and the main registry advance immediately. For example, restart_full on an inactive paused or interrupted qualified attempt is durably admitted, then rejected because the source is not invalidated. No next attempt is created, but neither runtime identity is restored. A subsequent valid resume runs the original attempt while progress requests target the nonexistent next attempt and controller exchanges for the actual attempt are rejected. Advance execution identity only when the next attempt exists, while retaining separate admission-action progress. Existing tests cover rejected resume followed by successful restart, but not rejected restart followed by valid resume.

findings.message: Approved restart cannot refresh the reviewer after artifact authorship changes.
findings.rationale: The prepare wrapper permanently binds the reviewer to the worker's initial reviewer. If an artifact's author changes during review, subject monitoring invalidates the attempt, but an explicit restart prepares the new independent reviewer and fails this equality check. The live public recover route reuses that worker and its original scope, so normal recovery cannot complete without externally retiring the worker. Preserve the guard by re-resolving main-owned reviewer authority and replacing the worker when necessary. The existing coordinator recovery test explicitly verifies reviewer refresh after an author change; the worker integration test never changes authorship and therefore misses this regression.

testCoverage.explanation: Completed the coverage review against all six acceptance checks using test bodies and assertions. Worker barriers establish durable admission before qualification/provider dispatch; route fixtures assert Epic, standalone and ISSUE ancestry and independent reviewer selection. Publication/history suites assert model-free replay and retained approval evidence. These positive assertions do not cover the three failing transitions identified in findings: cold public publication recovery, rejected restart followed by valid resume, or reviewer-changing restart through the worker registry. Verified describes completion of this inspection, not test execution.

findings.message: Apply permanent CR capability checks to post-cleanup progress reads.

Reuse equivalent version/capability validation and cover unsupported and mismatched versions through storedProgress after cleanup; current worker-cleanup assertions cover supported records only.
